title: Attention kernel optimization profiling — FlashAttention vs paged attention vs fused ops (experiments Feb 2026)
content:
Summary:
We ran a focused set of microbenchmarks and end-to-end inference checks to compare three attention implementations used/considered by the serving runtime: FlashAttention (baseline lib), paged attention (KV-page caching + tiled attention), and fused ops (custom fused matmul+softmax+dropout kernels). Goal was to characterize latency, p95 tail behavior, tokens/sec, and dominant GPU-side bottlenecks across sequence lengths and batching patterns typical of production traffic.

Background & motivation:
- Attention bottlenecks are the largest single kernel cost for medium/long context LLMs (8k+ tokens for 13B–70B families).
- We need to decide which kernel stack to standardize for Dedicated and Private runtimes where throughput/latency tradeoffs matter.
- Past work (see linked PR) implemented a prototype fused op and an experimental paged attention layer; this doc collates profiling runs and recommended next steps.

Environments tested:
- HW: NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe) and H100 80GB SXM.
- CUDA toolchain: CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.x, NCCL 2.18, driver 535.x.
- Framework: PyTorch 2.3 + torch.compile for microbench harnesses; custom C++ kernels loaded via Triton / C++ extensions for fused ops.
- Models: Llama-2-13B (fp16) trimmed to 2048/4096/8192 token windows; also a 70B variant for one long-context check.
- Quantization: tests primarily fp16; small set with 4-bit quantized weights using GPTQ to confirm kernel behavior under reduced-precision.

Methodology:
- Microbench harness implemented to run identical input batches through three kernel paths. Each run: 200 warmup steps + 1000 measured steps. Reported metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies (ms) per token, tokens/sec, GPU SM utilization, memory bandwidth (GB/s), and kernel launch counts.
- Tools: nsight-sys captures for timeline, nvprof-style per-kernel summaries via CUPTI trace processed with our perf parsing scripts, and torch.profiler for op-level breakdowns.
- Traffic patterns: single-stream low-qps (batch=1) for latency targets; steady throughput batches (batch=8,16) for throughput targets; mixed bursts to expose tail effects and KV cache interactions.

Key configs compared:
- FlashAttention (v2.0): upstream library, optimized kernels for grouped q/k/v with tiled softmax.
- Paged attention: runtime-managed KV pages (4k token pages), attention computes only on active pages, reduces memory traffic for long contexts but adds page management overhead.
- Fused ops: manually fused matmul+scale+mask+softmax+matmul kernels to reduce kernel-launch overhead and intermediate writes. Implemented as Triton kernels for fp16 and specialized for common head sizes (64).

Results (summary):
- Short context (<=2048 tokens), batch=1:
  - FlashAttention: p50 12.6 ms, p95 15.8 ms, tokens/s ~2800, SM util 62% on A100.
  - Fused ops: p50 11.1 ms, p95 13.9 ms, tokens/s ~3180, SM util 68%.
  - Paged attention: p50 14.4 ms, p95 19.2 ms (page check overhead dominates), tokens/s ~2450.
- Medium context (4096 tokens), batch=1:
  - FlashAttention: p50 26.7 ms, p95 35.1 ms, tokens/s ~1550.
  - Fused ops: p50 22.4 ms, p95 29.0 ms, tokens/s ~1850.
  - Paged attention: p50 24.2 ms, p95 33.8 ms, tokens/s ~1700 (benefit starts to appear but page lookup jitter increases tail).
- Long context (8192 tokens), batch=1:
  - FlashAttention: p50 62.1 ms, p95 88.7 ms, tokens/s ~700.
  - Fused ops: p50 48.9 ms, p95 64.0 ms, tokens/s ~950.
  - Paged attention: p50 41.7 ms, p95 79.5 ms, tokens/s ~1100 (avg throughput higher but p95 still high due to page fetch path).
- Throughput patterns (batch=16, 4096 context, A100):
  - FlashAttention throughput ~95 tokens/s per GPU (aggregate showed higher kernel parallelism but increased memory traffic).
  - Fused ops throughput +18% over FlashAttention.
  - Paged attention throughput +32% over FlashAttention when cache hit rate >80%, but sensitive to cache miss bursts.

Cross-HW notes (H100):
- H100 shows similar relative gains for fused ops vs FlashAttention but with reduced absolute latencies thanks to DPX and TensorFloat-32 improvements. Fused ops benefit slightly more on H100 due to better kernel launch throughput.

Profiling observations & bottleneck analysis:
- Kernel launch overhead: For low-batch, short-context p95, incremental cost of multiple small kernels (FlashAttention inner kernels + separate softmax) contributes ~12–18% of time. Fused ops reduces kernel launches and intermediate global memory writes which explains lower p95 and higher SM util.
- Memory bandwidth vs compute: For long contexts, memory bandwidth (KV reads/writes) dominates; paged attention reduces total memory reads when page hits are high. Measured bandwidth shows paged path lower sustained GB/s on long contexts with good locality.
- Page management jitter: Paged attention introduces CPU-GPU synchronization points when fetching new pages -> spikes in p95. These spikes correlate with page miss events in the timeline captures.
- Softmax numerics and stability: Our fused softmax kernel had to implement a stable exp-sum trick; initial naive fusion produced small numeric diffs (~1e-3 logits) vs upstream which are acceptable but flagged by some eval tests. Need extended eval on QA metrics before ramp.
- Occupancy: Fused kernels achieve higher SM occupancy consistently; FlashAttention sometimes underutilizes SMs for uncommon head sizes (48) due to non-optimal tiling.

Recommendations:
1) Short-term (next 2 sprints): adopt fused ops in the main inference path for fp16 13B–70B families on Dedicated nodes where we control runtime kernels. Benefits: consistent latency improvements and better p95. Action: merge PR #452 after numeric regression test and add feature flag.
2) Medium-term: keep paged attention as an opt-in path for very long contexts (>=8k) when workloads show high locality. But we must:
   - Reduce page miss synchronization by prefetching (asynchronous page loads via CUDA streams) and avoid CPU stalls.
   - Add page eviction heuristics tuned by workload (LRU with recency bias).
3) Testing & safety: run extended A/B evaluation on canary fleet (Dedicated) for 2 weeks comparing fused ops vs FlashAttention on real traffic. Monitor quality metrics (perplexity, end-user QA regressions) and p95 latency regressions.
4) Kernel maintenance: upstream contributions to FlashAttention remain important; continue collaborating to fold some fused patterns upstream to reduce divergence.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Evaluate fused ops impact on 4-bit quantized inference (triton kernels need adjustments).
- Test paged attention with HBM prefetching patterns on H100 to confirm reduced p95 when stream overlap is tuned.
- Explore hybrid: use fused ops for in-page compute + paged KV to combine benefits.

Action items:
- Priya: finalize numeric stability tests for fused softmax and add deterministic debug mode (due 2026-02-28).
- Miguel: implement async page prefetch prototype and run 1k-run microbench on H100 (due 2026-03-05).
- Alex: prepare canary rollout plan + instrumentation for perf/quality tracking (due 2026-03-03).

Appendix: links to captures and raw outputs:
- Nsight traces: perf dashboard link in metadata.
- Raw microbench results CSV: https://perf.redwood-internal/exports/attention-kernel/2026-02/raw-results.csv
- GitHub PR with fused kernel code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/452

Notes (informal):
- Observed a weird stall once on A100 during paged-attention runs — turned out to be a bad page alignment in the prototype allocator, fixed in local branch.
- Some short-context latency wins may be sensitive to head-size distribution across models; keep experiments per-head-size when we expand matrix.

Concluding statement:
Fused ops provide the clearest immediate win for latency-sensitive production workloads; paged attention is promising for long-context throughput but needs prefetching and reduced synchronization to be safe for low-latency SLAs. Recommend canary rollout of fused ops with feature flag, while continuing engineering effort on paged attention for targeted long-context use cases.
